title: api: unify rate-limit semantics, idempotency keys, Retry-After handling, and OpenAI compat error codes
author: Evelyn Chen
description: Motivation: We observed inconsistency in how rate limits, idempotency collisions, and streaming errors were surfaced through the OpenAI compatibility layer. Different endpoints and runtimes returned different 429 bodies, sometimes omitted Retry-After, and streaming sessions could terminate without a standard terminal error event, making client retries and backoff fragile. What this PR does: 1) Adds a centralized rate-limit middleware that normalizes all rate-limited responses to HTTP 429 with a standard JSON body: {"error":{"type":"rate_limit_error","message":"Quota exceeded: try again later","code":"rate_limit_exceeded"}} and emits a Retry-After header in seconds when available. 2) Implements idempotency-key handling for POST endpoints under the OpenAI compat paths (/v1/completions, /v1/chat/completions, /v1/outputs). If a request includes X-Idempotency-Key we persist the request fingerprint and final response for a configurable window (default 24h). Duplicate requests within the window return the original response with header Idempotency-Status: replay and Idempotency-Window-Remaining in seconds. 3) Streaming stability: streaming sessions now include a final terminal event for errors (type: "error") sent as an SSE/stream message so clients see a consistent terminal shape across recoverable and non-recoverable failures. Rate-limit events mid-stream include Retry-After data and a 429 terminal chunk when appropriate. 4) OpenAI compatibility mapping: centralized error mapping layer maps internal error classes to OpenAI-style error objects (type, message, code) to provide stable cross-client semantics. 5) Backwards-compatibility and rollout: behavior is backward-compatible for well-behaved clients; previously malformed 429 bodies are now standardized which may require clients that parse legacy shapes to adapt. Feature flag api.error_unification was added to allow staged rollout. 6) Observability and testing: added metrics for idempotency hits/misses, rate-limit counters per-route, and integration+streaming tests that validate Retry-After, idempotency replays, and terminal error events. Migration notes: Clients should retry on 429 using Retry-After when present; if using idempotency keys, expect a replay response rather than a 409. For long-running streaming consumers, handle the final error event as the authoritative terminal state. Implementation details: rate-limit middleware hooks into the existing token bucket implementation and surfaces server-suggested backoff windows; idempotency store is implemented on top of existing durable cache (redis) with an opaque stored response payload; OpenAI compat layer performs error code mapping at the last serialization step. Testing: unit tests for middleware, integration tests that simulate quota exhaustion, and streaming e2e tests for mid-stream rate limits. Rollout plan: enable flag in staging for 48h, then gradual rollout to 25% of traffic, 50%, then 100% while monitoring rate-limit and idempotency metrics.

compat: add OpenAI error mapping layer and standardize error shape
idempotency: record and replay responses for X-Idempotency-Key requests
streaming: emit terminal error events and include Retry-After in streaming protocol
tests: add integration + streaming tests and idempotency unit tests
docs: update API docs and migration notes

release_notes: Standardize API error shapes and rate-limit semantics across OpenAI compatibility endpoints. Add server-side idempotency key handling for POST endpoints, consistent Retry-After headers, and stable streaming terminal error events. Backwards-compatible with migration notes in docs.
